newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria has preliminary 21.4 bln lev 96 trade gap.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria has preliminary 21.4 bln lev 96 trade gap.

text.p: Bulgaria posted a trade deficit of 21.4 billion levs last year after a 28.6 billion lev surplus in 1995, the National Statistics Institute said, quoting preliminary customs figures.
Bulgaria posted a 101.9 billion lev trade surplus in the first nine months of 1996, the NSI said.

"Despite the sharp lev fall Bulgaria did not post a trade surplus because industrial production fell due to shrinking demand and strong dependence on imported raw materials and fuels," a NSI official who declined to be named told Reuters.
Trade figures in US dollars reported by the Bulgarian National Bank would be available in May.
Industrial goods accounted for 39.1 percent of Bulgaria's total exports and 29.3 percent of imports last year.
Consumer goods made up 18.2 percent of total exports and 5.6 percent of imports.
Fuels and lubricants had the largest share in last year's imports with 36.1 percent. Their share in total exports was 7.9 percent.

Bulgarian exports to member countries of Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development had the largest share of total exports with 424.4 billion levs. Bulgarian imports from those countries totalled 359.4 billion levs.
Imports from Central and Eastern European countries made the bulk of total Bulgarian imports last year with 422.4 billion levs. Exports to those countries amounted to 261.4 billion levs.
Total trade turnover for 1996 amounted to 1,723.9 billion levs at current prices, down a real 14.5 percent from 1995, figures showed.
The lev fell to around 500 per dollar at end-1996 from 70 at the beginning of the year.
Industrial production fell a real 3.3 percent in 1996 year on year due to delayed economic restructuring and mismanagement by the former Socialist government. -- Sofia Newsroom, (++359-2) 911 88
